chapter_theme: The body linga: the form of the human body is the Sivalinga, Chidambaram, Sadasiva and the holy dance. The Lord enters the body as his temple, the five keep its gates, and the worship he takes there is made by setting the senses behind.

1726.reading: The form of the human body is the Sivalinga, the form of the human body is Chidambaram, the form of the human body is Sadasiva, and the form of the human body is the holy dance.
1726.nuance: The refrain மானுடர் ஆக்கை வடிவு claims the body's very shape (வடிவு), not only what dwells in it. Chidambaram is the hall where Siva dances, and the verse puts the hall, the dancer, the dance and the linga all in the human frame.

1727.reading: Those who have not wasted away stand as though they live on; so, as earth, water and the rest that make the flesh become one with the five elements and the senses, worship the Lord who gives strength.
1727.nuance: The first two lines are obscure. உலந்திலர் may be those who have not died, perhaps the perfected who keep their bodies, and நிலந்திரு நீர்தெளி ஊன் may list the elements that make the flesh. வலந்தரு may mean 'who gives strength' or 'circumambulated'. The plain thrust is that the body made of the five elements is where worship is done.

1728.reading: When he took the body as his temple the five took up dwelling there, and keeping its gates they guide and give grace; the Master entered me as if taken into a mother, took the gate, and came to rule me.
1728.nuance: The five (ஐவர்) may be the five deities who govern the body in Siddhanta or the five senses turned to the Lord's service. தாயில் கொண்டாற்போல் is unclear: as a child is held in its mother, or as a mother takes in her child. வாயில் (gate) recurs in 1729.

1729.reading: Our great Nandi took the body as his temple, with the great Veda as the ground of his feet and the ten nadis as its gates, and took its worship once the five senses were put behind.
1729.nuance: கொல்லைப் பெருமறை (the great Veda of the field) is obscure. The ten nadis are traditionally the body's main channels of breath. புலன் ஐந்தும் பிறகிட்டு (the five senses set behind) makes the worship itself an act of restraint.

links.note: On what the human body is: the Naladiyar breaks it into entrails, fat, blood, bone and sinew and asks which part is the beautiful woman; Tirumular says the body's very form is the Sivalinga, Chidambaram and Siva's dance. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar's verse is read as a verdict on the body and not only as a remedy for desire.
1823, in the chapter on Siva worship, makes the heart the temple, the body the shrine and the soul the linga; 1726 goes further and makes the body's own form the linga.

Both speak of the five senses as gates (வாயில்) to be mastered. The Kural praises the one who quenched the five sense-gates and the long life of those who follow him; Tirumular has Nandi enter the body by its gates and receive worship once the senses are put behind.

1728 has the body as the Lord's temple, with the five keeping its gates (வாயில்கொண்டு) and giving grace. 1823 builds the whole temple: heart the sanctum, body the shrine, mouth the tower gate (வாய்கோபுரவாசல்), and the five thieving senses its lamps (கள்ளப் புலன்ஐந்தும் காளா மணிவிளக்கே). Both turn the five from enemies into servants of the indwelling Lord; 1823 maps every part of the temple onto the body.

source_issues: 1727: lines 1 and 2 (உலந்திலர் பின்னும் உளரென நிற்பர் / நிலந்திரு நீர்தெளி யூனவை செய்ய) are obscure and may be corrupt.
